title: Justified Access Cards & Temporal Grants — Review Hub and Policy Diff Heatmap
creator: Ava Morales
description: Design a compact, review-focused UI for org and workspace access reviews that blends three concepts: 1) Justified Access Cards — short, scannable cards showing who has access, why (justification), and a one-click revoke/appeal action; 2) Temporal Grant Snapshots — lightweight timeline snapshots that let reviewers inspect when a grant was created, last used, and expired; and 3) Policy Diff Heatmap — visual diffs that surface recent role/policy changes across workspaces and the estimated cost impact of a role change (approx. token/compute cost delta) for model-serving roles. The goal is to lower friction for compliance auditors and platform engineers to triage access, approve rollbacks, and correlate permission changes with spike in inference cost or rollouts. This ticket covers end-to-end flow: discovery, low-fidelity and hi-fidelity prototypes, accessibility review, and handoff artifacts for engineering.
acceptance_criteria:
- Prototype (Figma) includes: review hub landing, Justified Access Card component, expanded Temporal Grant timeline, Policy Diff Heatmap panel, and an empty-state for no outstanding reviews.
- Usability test (n>=6 internal reviewers) showing median time-to-decision <= 90s on a sampled 5-item access queue.
- Accessibility checklist completed (labels, focus order, color-contrast).
- Engineering handoff: component spec, interaction states, copy, and an integration notes doc linking to ENG-12790 and ENG-12810.
- Product sign-off from PM (Samira Patel) and Security (security@redwood.ai).
comments: 2026-02-20 — Kickoff: Aligned goals with PM (Samira) and Eng leads (Kai, Luca). Scope prioritized to org + workspace level; cross-workspace rollups deferred to follow-up. Noted dependency on ENG-12790 (audit event indexing) and ENG-12810 (cost attribution API).

2026-02-25 — Iteration 1: Low-fi cards created. Design decision: show up to three justification snippets inline, link to full audit stream for deeper context. PM requested a visible 'confidence' indicator for automated role assignments (low/medium/high).
2026-03-01 — Security review (initial): Security team requested retention indicator and explicit KMS/audit token references when showing last-accessed events. Added note to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-05 — Usability test (internal, n=6): Observations: reviewers liked compact cards but missed quick filtering by 'cost impact'. Adjusted Policy Diff Heatmap to include a small histogram of estimated token delta. Median time-to-decision: 82s.
2026-03-09 — Design critique: Feedback from Design Org: simplify action menu (revoke/appeal/acknowledge) and add confirmation microcopy to reduce accidental revokes. Added error/undo state mockups.
2026-03-12 — Eng sync: Backend team can return precomputed 'cost_delta' per role starting 2026-03-20; front-end will need a placeholder until API ready. Handoff planned 2026-03-18.
decisions: Justified Access Cards will prioritize scannability: name, role, one-line justification, last-used timestamp, and cost_delta badge.
Temporal Grant Snapshots default to 'last 90 days' with quick jumps to creation event and most recent use.
Policy Diff Heatmap uses workspace rows x role columns, color intensity maps to number of changed bindings; hover reveals a mini-diff + estimated cost impact.
Primary action for reviewers is 'Revoke' with an inline 'Appeal' link that opens a modal tied to audit events; revoke is reversible via a 30s undo snackbar.
next_steps: Finalize hi-fi Figma screens and annotate component tokens (colors/spacing/typography).
Prepare engineering handoff bundle (design tokens, react component spec, interaction gifs) by 2026-03-18.
Schedule moderated usability sessions with 5 customer security champions (target week 2026-03-23).
Create E2E QA checklist and add to ENG-12790 and ENG-12810 PRs.
